messages.subject: Requesting Code Review of Model
parts:
I am a new user of lavaan and rarely use CFA in the work I do. I'm having to dust off some old notes on the topic. I am fitting models using lavaan and am requesting a review of my code to make sure I am fitting the model I think I am fitting. My email below is organized to show 1) Background 2) R code 3) Questions.

Background

I have 50 dichotomously scored test items (1=correct response, 0 = otherwise) and various items are presumed to load onto different dimensions. My research objective is to test the hypothesized multidimensional structure of the test against a simple baseline model assuming all items load onto a single dimension.

The multidimensional model I want to estimate is a second order model where items load onto the first order factors and then those first order factors load onto a common factor. The second order factors would all share a pairwise correlation.

R Code

The code I am using is below. I want the polychoric correlations; hence the use of the ordered() function. Additionally, I want to identify the model by fixing the variance of the latent variables to 1, which I believe is accomplished via the 'std.lv = TRUE' argument. Also, because I am a novice with this package I am using the cfa() function in lieu of the lavaan() function which I understand to be slightly more advanced.

model <- '
Rep1_KID =~ X20748 + X17553 + X20851 + X19461 + X19478 + X20377 + X20376 + X20378 + X14245 + X14106 + X14116 + X14244

Rep2_CS =~ X14383 + X20753 + X17575 + X19982 + X17544 + X19984 + X17569 + X20765 + X20758 + X20766 + X19450 + X19474 + X19447 + X20373 + X20372 + X14145 + X20368 + X14168 + X14170 + X14248 + X20853 + X14130 + X14256

Rep3_IKI =~ X18934 + X18707 + X18709 + X20365 + X14151 + X14167 + X14218

Rep4_LE =~ X19087 + X19089 + X18695 + X18697 + X18683 + X18684 + X18685 + X18686

trait =~ Rep1_KID + Rep2_CS + Rep3_IKI + Rep4_LE'

fit1 <- cfa(model, tmp, ordered = names(tmp), std.lv = TRUE)

Questions

My first question is basic. Does my R code reflect the model I intend to estimate as I describe in the background?

My suspicion is no for two reasons. First, the output I get from the model is junk (all loadings are about 0) and I do not see any covariances between the second order factors in the summary() output.

If instead I use the same model code but DROP this portion

trait =~ Rep1_KID + Rep2_CS + Rep3_IKI + Rep4_LE

then the output all seems very reasonable, but the structure then doesn't match what I think I want to estimate.

Again, thank you for your support. I am not new to R, but new to this group and if I have missed any common protocols as we typically require on the R listserve I am happy to update and provide that information

Harold

parts:
Maybe the parameters can't be estimated because the sample size is too small compared to the amount of noise in the data. That's just a guess; the more knowledgeable people here might be able to give a better explanation.

I still don't know what you meant by correlations among second order factors. I think your code is ok though, because the following example works:

set.seed(1)

n <- 300

G <- rnorm(n)

beta1 <- 0.7
beta2 <- 0.6
beta3 <- 0.5

F1 <- beta1*G + rnorm(n, 0, sqrt(1 - beta1^2))
F2 <- beta2*G + rnorm(n, 0, sqrt(1 - beta2^2))
F3 <- beta3*G + rnorm(n, 0, sqrt(1 - beta3^2))

# Loadings
c11 <- 0.7
c12 <- 0.7
c13 <- 0.6
c14 <- 0.5
c21 <- 0.6
c22 <- 0.6
c23 <- 0.6
c31 <- 0.8
c32 <- 0.7
c33 <- 0.7

d <- data.frame(v11 = c11*F1 + rnorm(n, 0, sqrt(1 - c11^2)),
                v12 = c12*F1 + rnorm(n, 0, sqrt(1 - c12^2)),
                v13 = c13*F1 + rnorm(n, 0, sqrt(1 - c13^2)),
                v14 = c14*F1 + rnorm(n, 0, sqrt(1 - c14^2)),
                v21 = c21*F2 + rnorm(n, 0, sqrt(1 - c21^2)),
                v22 = c22*F2 + rnorm(n, 0, sqrt(1 - c22^2)),
                v23 = c23*F2 + rnorm(n, 0, sqrt(1 - c23^2)),
                v31 = c31*F3 + rnorm(n, 0, sqrt(1 - c31^2)),
                v32 = c32*F3 + rnorm(n, 0, sqrt(1 - c32^2)),
                v33 = c33*F3 + rnorm(n, 0, sqrt(1 - c33^2)))

for (j in 1:ncol(d)) {
  d[, sub("v", "x", names(d)[j])] <- ifelse(d[, j] > 0, 1, 0)
}
# the x variables are the dichotomised versions of the v variables

mod1 <- '
F1 =~ x11 + x12 + x13 + x14
F2 =~ x21 + x22 + x23
F3 =~ x31 + x32 + x33
G =~ F1 + F2 + F3
'

sem1 <- cfa(mod1, data=d, ordered=c("x11", "x12", "x13", "x14", "x21", "x22", "x23", "x31", "x32", "x33"),
            std.lv=TRUE)

sem1
parameterEstimates(sem1, standardized=TRUE)

# If you use a larger n (e.g. 10000 or 100000), the std.all estimates are close to the true values

I don't know what the problem is when fitting the model to your data. Do you get any warnings? Maybe the model is a really bad model for your data.

The correlations between visual, textual and speed are not model parameters because they're endogenous variables in that model. In the example I gave, you can use lavInspect(sem1, "cor.lv") to see the model-implied correlations among the latent variables. The help page for lavInspect() lists all the other stuff it can give you.

On 10/08/2015 09:40 PM, Mark Seeto wrote:
> I don't think the problem is your R code, because the example I gave is
> similar and it worked. Maybe someone else can give a suggestion.

I agree. There is nothing wrong with the R code. The second-order model
simply does not fit (your data). That is often the case.

Try to fit the model without the std.lv = TRUE flag, and I bet you will
get a different warning, something along the lines of:

Warning messages:
1: In lav_object_post_check(lavobject) :
lavaan WARNING: some estimated variances are negative
2: In lav_object_post_check(lavobject) :
lavaan WARNING: covariance matrix of latent variables is not positive
definite; use inspect(fit,"cov.lv") to investigate.

This warning is more informative (in the sense that it tells you that
the second-order model does not fit well), and by using std.lv=TRUE, we
force (residuals) variances to be unity, and this may be far from the truth.

Yves.
